message:
docs(release): cut the key folder's inheritance, and correct two things I asserted

The folder was inheriting an entry from %LOCALAPPDATA% for a SID that does
not resolve here, with write access. I wrote that up as a deleted account.
There was no basis for that: a SID fails to resolve when a domain is
unreachable or when it belongs to another machine, and this one's domain
part differs from this PC's user SID -- so somewhere that can resolve it may
well exist. Unresolvable is not the same as nobody, which is precisely why
the inheritance had to go.

Only the key folder and its files, as approved. %LOCALAPPDATA%, GNLink and
ReleaseSigning keep the permissions they had. Three explicit principals now:
the owning user, SYSTEM and Administrators. The original ACL was saved
before touching anything and is restored if any step fails -- getting this
wrong locks the owner out of a folder holding a DPAPI-protected private key.

Checked afterwards: the four files still read, the key still unprotects,
imports, signs and verifies against the recorded public hex (and still
rejects a tampered probe), and no principal outside the three appears on the
folder or on any file.

Also corrected: losing this key is not "sign again with a new one".
Installed products carry the old public key and will not trust a manifest
signed by a new one, so there is no update path back -- it means people
installing by hand and a trust transition. The backup question is still
open, and tightening an ACL does not answer it.
